faq.q: How do I make green paint?
faq.a: Mix yellow and blue. Start with yellow and add tiny amounts of blue: more yellow gives a bright lime green, more blue gives a deep green.

faq.q: How do I make purple paint?
faq.a: Mix blue and red. A cool red like crimson and a blue like ultramarine give a bright purple; adding white makes a lighter lilac.

faq.q: Why start with the lighter colour?
faq.a: Dark colours are strong, so a small dab changes a light colour a lot. Starting light and adding dark slowly saves paint and gives you more control.
asks: How do I stop my paint going too dark?

faq.q: Why does mixing all paints make brown?
faq.a: Each paint soaks up some colours of light and reflects the rest. Mix them all and together they soak up most of the light, leaving a dull dark brown.
asks: Why do my colours turn muddy?
What do all colours make together?

faq.q: Why is mixing light different from paint?
faq.a: Paint works by taking colours away from the light that hits it, so mixing makes it darker. Light adds colours together, so red, green and blue light make white.
asks: What are the primary colours of light?
Why do red and green light make yellow?

facts: Mixing red, green and blue light in equal amounts produces white light.
In painting, yellow and blue mix to make green, red and yellow make orange, and red and blue make purple.

quiz.say: You want orange paint for a pumpkin. Which two colours do you mix?
What happens when you mix red, yellow and blue paint all together?
quiz.why: Mixed paints soak up most of the light between them, leaving a dark brown.

wrong.1: White comes from mixing coloured light, not paint.
wrong.2: Mixing blends colours into one; it does not separate them.
